goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about calling Optional.get() without checking isPresent(), and about unsafe raw List deserialization. C2 is about the stored credential data having an unexpected format, which is a different problem. No candidate raises the empty-Optional risk.

goldens.comment: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
goldens.reasoning: C1 says the same thing as G2: createFromValues leaves the id unset, so removal by id breaks.

candidates: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) doesn't set an id, so the credential returned from getCredentials() will have a null id; this can break flows that rely on credential IDs (e.g., removal via removeStoredCredentialById)

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() can return credentials from user storage (CredentialInputUpdater#getCredentials); if those CredentialModels don't have credentialData/secretData in Keycloak's expected JSON format, the subsequent RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(...) will throw at runtime and break login

Recovery-code validation accepts any stored code and never consumes/removes it, which makes recovery codes reusable and ignores the sequential 'code #N' behavior enforced by RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider

TestAppHelper.logout() relies on refreshToken set by completeLogin(), but this test never calls completeLogin() after submitting the recovery code; logout may become a no-op and leave sessions behind for later tests
